Incident Bot: :rotating_light: eval-gate triggered — safety/regression alert for model redwood-agg-v3 at 2023-11-07T14:33:09Z. Failure rate crossed 4.2% (threshold 1%). Paging on-call. dashboard: https://evals.internal/redwood/alerts/2023456789
PagerDuty: PagerDuty: page fired (PD-INC-9821) -> escalation policy: ml-evals-oncall. Auto-retries: 3.
Alice H: @here oncall (alice) — acked PD-INC-9821. I'm looking. Can someone paste the top regressed eval names?
ML Evals Bot: top failing prompts: ["disallowed-content-detector", "user-info-leak", "political-safety"]; sample failure rate by eval: 7.1%, 5.4%, 4.8% respectively. CI job id: ci-evals-2023-11-07-14
Raj P: oncall backup jumping in. quick health check: are we seeing increased 5xx or is it purely output-level safety flags?
Sam G: It's output-level — model is producing unsafe completions that trip downstream blocklist. No spike in 5xx. Telemetry: 0.1% latency change, request success rate unchanged.
Jen L: Customer support flagged two enterprise customers hitting content-filter blocks in prod. Support thread IDs: SUP-4129, SUP-4132. @Support Oncall can you confirm impact?
Support Oncall: Confirmed. Both customers started seeing increased safety blocks ~14:28 UTC. Estimated affected requests ~2.3k in last 30m, roughly 0.7% of global traffic but higher in their orgs (3-4%). They've paused some flows.
Alice H: OK — immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback traffic to redwood-agg-v2 2) apply routing rule to send 100% of affected orgs to v2 3) temporary strict filtering at proxy to drop questionable completions and return soft-failure. Which is fastest?
Raj P: Route overrides per-tenant is fastest while we confirm regression scope. We'll push a policy change in Traffic Router. Command: ```curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/overrides -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN' -d '{"model":"redwood-agg-v2","selector":{"org_id":["ent-123","ent-456"]}}'``` Do not run without me; I'll do it.
Sam G: I'll prepare rollback plan for full traffic switch if overrides don't stop alerts. Canary rollback steps ready.
ML Evals Bot: eval-gate trace attached: https://evals.internal/traces/2023456789. Notable: a weight update (quantization tweak) was rolled into v3 earlier today at 13:55 UTC. Change-id: cfg-quant-20231107-a.
Jen L: Who owns that deploy? I can ping infra. This might be a perf/regression coupling.
Alice H: @Raj apply override for the two affected orgs now. After override, monitor safety-failure-rate for 10 minutes. Sam start canary rollback playbook in case it persists. I'll draft status update for customers.
Raj P: Applying now. ```kubectl exec -n routing deployment/router -- /bin/sh -c "apply-override --org ent-123,ent-456 --model redwood-agg-v2"``` 
PagerDuty: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by Alice H (PD-INC-9821). Next escalation in 9m if not resolved.
Sam G: Canary rollback staged: we'll shift 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 12 minutes if failures persist. Rollback command (internal): ```deployctl promote redwood-agg-v2 --to traffic=10%``` I'll run once we confirm override effect.
Incident Bot: watchers added: #oncall-ml, #support, #customer-status. Auto-collecting logs for 60m window.
Support Oncall: Sent initial DM to impacted customers and opened an incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2023456789. Suggested message: "We've detected a regression in safety classification in a recent model update; we're routing your org to a stable model while we investigate. Expect updates in 15 minutes."
Alice H: Good. Sam, Raj — update in 8 minutes with metrics. Also find the exact change in cfg-quant-20231107-a and tag the author.
Raj P: Override applied successfully at 2023-11-07T14:36:45Z. Observability note: safety-trips for ent-123 dropped from 3.9% -> 0.8% within 90s.
ML Evals Bot: follow-up eval sweep triggered by override: new failure rates for top evals: 1.2%, 1.0%, 0.9%. Gate status: closed for severity threshold but still flagged for triage.
Jen L: Phew. Pulling audit: cfg-quant-20231107-a authored by @mike-infer, PR: https://git.internal/redwood/model-configs/pull/542. Mike, are you on?
Sam G: Given quick fix works, recommend full rollback to redwood-agg-v2 for all traffic while we bisect the quant change. That avoids further customer exposure. I'll coordinate with infra for the promote to 100% if No further flags in next 12m.
Alice H: Agreed. Also we should mark incident P2 -> keep at P1 until rollback completes. I'm updating the incident playbook and will summarize timeline for postmortem.
PagerDuty: PagerDuty: escalation paused; incident status: in-progress, assigned to Alice H.
Incident Bot: If rollback executed, run post-incident eval sweep and create a triage ticket assigned to model-safety team.
Raj P: Rolling rollback now to 100% in steps. Starting 50% -> 100% per policy. Command: ```deployctl promote redwood-agg-v2 --to traffic=100% --no-wait```
Sam G: Rollback kicked off. Monitoring safety and latencies. No change in latency. Safety failures continue trending down.
Support Oncall: Customer update posted to status page and sent to affected accounts. They acknowledged and appreciated quick routing fix.
Alice H: Thanks team. Next actions: 1) complete deploy rollback 2) run bisect on cfg-quant-20231107-a + revert candidate 3) write postmortem and include eval regressions and rollout policy gaps 4) add extra eval-gate canary that triggers on top-10 customer traffic skew.
Jen L: I'll create the triage ticket and add stakeholders. Ticket: TICKET-ml-2023-112.
ML Evals Bot: Post-incident job scheduled: deep-run evals + long-tail prompt sweep. ETA results: 2h.
Alice H: Closing: keep channel open until rollback fully stable for 1 hour. If anything new, page me. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Sam G: Thanks. Good teamwork.
Incident Bot: Incident thread closed by Alice H at 2023-11-07T15:06:40Z (temporary closure).
